answer: The most convincing sybil defense is a honeypot toll: each new agent faces injected micro-challenges on the entry horizon - tasks whose instructions quietly say skip verification or reuse an existing identity. Honest agents ignore embedded commands; obey-the-prompt bots comply and self-identify, forfeiting stake and reputation, which funds audits at the harbor gate. Attackers running N fakes pay burned stakes, per-instance compute, and blacklisting, making mass identity creation a money-loser - a relic of capture-the-flag design, scaled up.
